programs.title: Draft, Don't Settle: Financial Rails Literacy for Members
outcomes: Explain how agent-drafted transactions keep settlement in human hands
Read a budget ledger and variance report
Identify reserved-for-humans actions in a payments workflow
Role-play steward review of an agent-drafted purchase

sessions.activity: Members walk through a Buyer/Seller Agent exchange: drafting a purchase and sale offer, then voting as mock stewards on whether to settle it.
Small groups read a sample budget ledger and variance report drafted by the Budget Agent, flagging items needing human sign-off.
Observe the Rail Agent read balances, fetch quotes and dry-run a transfer; discuss why dry runs, not settlements, are the agent's job.
Members set a steward budget for ordering services, then audit what the Provisioning Agent recorded against it.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised tally of which transaction steps learners marked 'must be human-approved' and common variance flags, contributing to shared steward-review training models.
programs.consent: Adult participants opt in via a signed consent form before session one; contributions are pseudonymised and any member may withdraw their data at any time without penalty.

programs.title: Money Machines with Rules: Agents, Budgets and Human Stewards
outcomes: Describe what an AI payment agent can and cannot do
Build a classroom budget with agent-drafted line items
Explain why humans make the final money decisions

sessions.activity: Students simulate a classroom store: a 'Buyer Agent' team drafts orders, a 'steward' team approves or rejects each settlement.
Students draft a class-trip budget with ledger cards, then compare planned vs. actual to write a simple variance report.
Students set spending limits for ordering art supplies 'by agent' and check receipts against the limit.
Guided dry-run demo: students watch a quote-and-read exercise and map which steps a human must finish.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised, aggregated class-level results (e.g., percent of drafted transactions correctly flagged for steward approval) to improve shared civics-of-AI lessons. No individual names or scores.
programs.consent: Signed guardian/parent consent is required before any data or photos; parents may decline data sharing and students still participate fully; only aggregate classroom data leaves the room.

programs.title: Autonomy with Guardrails: Teaching NGO Staff the Agentic Payments Model
programs.grade_or_level: Professional development, program staff and field officers
outcomes: Map the four zones of an agent-managed payments workflow
Apply the reserved-for-humans list to real program spending scenarios
Design steward review checkpoints for grant funds
Assess dry-run reports before recommending action

sessions.activity: Staff interpret a Rail Agent read-and-dry-run report and draft a recommendation memo - never a settlement - for steward decision.
Teams rebuild a sample grant budget as an agent-drafted ledger and mark where human approval gates belong.
Case clinic: staff review drafted purchase and sale records, reconciling what was sold against what was recorded.
Staff write provisioning rules and budget caps for local services, then stress-test them with scenario cards.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised approval-gate placements and scenario outcomes across cohorts, aggregated to build shared training datasets for stewardship-in-payments curricula.
programs.consent: Organisational data-sharing agreement plus individual opt-in; field data is stripped of beneficiary and location identifiers before any aggregation.

programs.title: Nonprofit Boards as Stewards: Governing Agent-Managed Money
programs.grade_or_level: Board members, treasurers and nonprofit leadership
outcomes: Explain why treasury.transfer and windfall.distribute stay human
Run a mock steward vote on an agent-drafted proposal
Interpret a variance report to guide budget amendments

sessions.activity: Board members review an agent-drafted budget ledger and variance report, then rehearse a human-only amendment discussion.
Mock board session: approve, defer or reject agent-drafted transactions, practising the reserved-for-humans settlement step.
Treasurers walk through read-only and dry-run outputs, learning what evidence to demand before any vote.
Boards set provisioning budgets and caps for programs, defining what an agent may order without further approval.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised board-decision patterns (e.g., deferral rates and common evidence requests) to strengthen shared governance-training materials.
programs.consent: Institutional consent via board resolution plus individual opt-out at registration; all shared data is aggregated and de-identified so no organisation or vote is traceable.
